name: PF-07220060
summary: PF-07220060 is atirmociclib, Pfizer's oral CDK4-selective inhibitor (discovered in house) and the intended successor to Ibrance. The pivotal trial is FourLight-3 (NCT06760637): open-label Phase 3, about 1,020 to 1,035 adults with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease, randomised 1:1 to atirmociclib 300 mg twice daily plus letrozole against investigator's choice of CDK4/6 inhibitor plus letrozole. The primary endpoint is PFS by blinded central review, and primary completion is 2029-01-02. Price anchor: Ibrance, Pfizer's own first-line CDK4/6 inhibitor with letrozole, at $127,804 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: Kisqali, the third CDK4/6 entrant, held 24.4% of 2024 CDK4/6 Part D beneficiaries.

therapy_mode.source: FourLight-3 design (NCT06760637; ESMO 2025 624TiP, Annals of Oncology, https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)01966-0/fulltext): atirmociclib 300 mg by mouth twice daily, continuously in 28-day cycles, with letrozole, PFS primary endpoint
therapy_mode.note: Oncology treated to progression, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table (ClinicalTrials.gov v2 pull 2026-09-24) for NCT06760637: PF-07220060 with letrozole against palbociclib, ribociclib or abemaciclib (trial_interventions), primary outcome 'Progression Free Survival (PFS) by BICR', 1,035 enrolled, primary completion 2029-01-02 estimated. Continuous dosing to progression makes it chronic. The 300 mg twice-daily dose in the source text was not independently checked (Annals TiP page unreachable, web search budget spent); the verdict does not depend on it

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Ibrance: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $2,035,022,061 over 15,923 beneficiaries = $127,804 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator, under the house convention. Ibrance with letrozole is the first-line regimen in FourLight-3's control arm, Pfizer's own oral CDK inhibitor, and the drug atirmociclib is built to replace. The case against: the other two comparators in the same arm run lower per beneficiary in 2024: Verzenio $94,026 and Kisqali $88,305. Ibrance's figure is highest partly because its patients are longer on therapy. Ibrance was also selected for Medicare price negotiation (maximum fair price from 2027), so its gross figure will overstate what the class nets in Medicare by the time atirmociclib launches. Taking Kisqali instead would cut the price by 31%. No published annual list price for atirmociclib exists
list_price_per_patient.check: lookup.py demand Ibrance: Part D 2024 $2,035,022,061 / 15,923 beneficiaries = $127,804, so 0.127804 mm USD per patient-year. Kisqali $88,305 and Verzenio $94,026 in 2024 also reproduce, so the 31% cut quoted in the note (88,305/127,804 = 0.69) holds. Comparator choice is a flagged judgement; Ibrance is in the FourLight-3 control arm

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS per-beneficiary price (halving lands at a median 96% of CMS negotiated net prices; backend/gross_to_net.py), as the PF-07248144 and camizestrant seeds take it
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is $63,902 per patient-year. Manufacturer rebates in a crowded three-brand Part D class
gross_to_net_pct.check: Direction checked: 0.5 is share off list; 0.127804 x 0.5 = 0.063902, net $63,902 as stated. Matches the house convention and the PF-07248144 seed row (0.5, 'share off list', backend/gross_to_net.py)

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: PALOMA-2 (Finn et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:1925-36, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1607303): median PFS 24.8 months for palbociclib plus letrozole in first-line ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer, the control regimen of FourLight-3
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/24.8) = 0.285, the form the PF-07248144 and vepugratinib seeds use. The brief's 1 - exp(-12/24.8) gives 0.384; it treats the median as a mean, so not used. The case against: real-world time on first-line CDK4/6 plus AI is shorter than trial PFS (toxicity stops, older patients), which would raise this; and if atirmociclib beats the control arm, as it is designed to, duration would lengthen and lower it. MONARCH-3 (abemaciclib) reported 28.2 months, which gives 0.255
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed PMID 27959613 (Finn et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:1925-36, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1607303): median PFS 24.8 months (95% CI 22.1 to NE) for palbociclib-letrozole in untreated ER+/HER2- advanced disease. 1 - 0.5^(12/24.8) = 0.2849; MONARCH-3 alternative 1 - 0.5^(12/28.2) = 0.2554, arithmetic holds. Half-life form matches the PF-07248144 seed. Note: PALOMA-2 PFS was investigator-assessed, FourLight-3's is BICR

forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. Readout in early 2029, filing mid-2029, and a standard review puts US launch around mid-2030, so 2031 is the first full year. This matches the book's convention for PF-07248144: first full year two calendar years after primary completion. A priority review or an interim PFS analysis could pull the launch into late 2029 or early 2030
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials row NCT06760637: primary completion 2029-01-02 (estimated), last update 2026-05-19. PF-07248144 seed convention (first full year two calendar years after primary completion) gives 2031

exus_multiple.source: Ibrance FY2025: $1,412mm International against $2,710mm US (Pfizer 10-K 0000078003-26-000026, product revenue table), the ratio the PF-07248144 seed already carries
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator: Ibrance is the direct predecessor, sold by Pfizer on worldwide rights in the same setting. The case against: Ibrance's mature ex-US share is depressed by generic palbociclib in some markets and by Kisqali's ex-US strength, and a 2030s launch will face early ex-US generic CDK4/6 pricing

economics_share.source: Atirmociclib was designed and discovered at Pfizer (Discovery of Atirmociclib (PF-07220060), J Med Chem 2025, doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5c02137); Pfizer is lead sponsor of NCT06760637 and NCT04557449
economics_share.note: No partner, licence or royalty in Pfizer's filings (second reader checked the FY2025 10-K)
economics_share.check: Read the filings directly in the book's filing_sections. FY2025 10-K (0000078003-26-000026) late-stage table lists 'atirmociclib (PF-07220060) 1st line HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer' with no footnote letter; the table's footnotes (a)-(e) name Astellas (Padcev), Valneva (VLA15), RemeGen (disitamab vedotin) and nothing for atirmociclib. FY2024 10-K (0000078003-25-000054) lists it in 1st and 2nd line without a footnote either, while footnoting Alliance Foundation Trials, BMS, Astellas, Valneva, Arvinas, RemeGen. Searched every 'royalt*' occurrence in the FY2025 10-K and both 2026 10-Qs (0000078003-26-000054, -000095) for proximity to CDK, breast, palbociclib, Ibrance or atirmociclib: none. The 2026-05-05 8-K (0000078003-26-000053) reports FOURLIGHT-1 as Pfizer's own. PubMed PMID 41347260 (J Med Chem 2025;68:26085, doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5c02137): discovered by Pfizer La Jolla, all authors Pfizer. No royalty found

eligible_pct.source: Goyal et al., Breast Cancer Res Treat 2023;198:159-166 (doi:10.1007/s10549-022-06845-4; PMID 36609900), SEER-Medicare: all 3,244 women with HR+/HER2- MBC initiated first-line therapy, and chemotherapy (alone or combined) was 15.7% of first-line use over 2010-2019. 1 - 0.157 = 0.843 start on endocrine-based first-line therapy, the setting a CDK inhibitor plus letrozole serves
eligible_pct.note: Judgement on the filter. The label will reach first-line endocrine-based candidates. The case for a lower figure: the 0.843 includes endocrine monotherapy for frail patients and patients relapsing within a year of adjuvant aromatase inhibitor, who would take fulvestrant rather than letrozole. I found no US source for either share. The window also ends in 2019, when chemotherapy use was falling. Applied to incidence this is about 54,800 first-line starts a year. Applied to the book's 160,000 prevalence it gives an opening stock of 134,900, most of whom are already on a CDK4/6 inhibitor or past first line. See untreated_carryover_pct. Second reader: the Goyal cohort is women aged 65 and over (median 74) selected on initiating systemic therapy, so 0.843 is a share of treated older patients, not of every incident case; younger patients are likelier to get a CDK4/6 inhibitor and less likely to be untreated, which cut in opposite directions
eligible_pct.check: PubMed PMID 36609900 abstract (Goyal et al., Breast Cancer Res Treat 2023;198:159-166, doi:10.1007/s10549-022-06845-4): 3,244 women, all initiated first-line therapy; chemotherapy alone or combined 15.7% in first line over 2010-2019. 1 - 0.157 = 0.843. Age restriction (65+) added to the note. 65,000 x 0.843 = 54,795 first-line starts a year, as stated

untreated_carryover_pct.source: forecast.py (the engine), branch for a stated carryover of 0: 'No carryover means the eligible patients are each year's own, so the living stock is not an opening pool either'
untreated_carryover_pct.note: Kept at 0.0. The book's pool is the whole metastatic prevalence (160,000) and this is a first-line drug: a patient not started on atirmociclib in her first-line year takes another CDK4/6 inhibitor for about two years and leaves the line. With 0.0 stated, the engine now sets the opening pool to zero and treats each year's eligible diagnoses (65,000 x 0.843 = about 54,800) as the pool, so year one is no longer overstated. The researcher's earlier warning about the opening stock no longer applies
untreated_carryover_pct.check: Value unchanged. Source corrected: the book holds no untreated_carryover_pct row for vepugratinib or any other asset (assumptions table searched), so the cited precedent does not hold; re-sourced to the engine's own convention in backend/forecast.py, which on a stated 0 zeroes the opening pool. Note rewritten to drop the out-of-date year-one warning

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible untreated patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: lookup.py demand, CMS Part D 2024 beneficiaries: Kisqali 8,782 of the three-brand CDK4/6 total of 35,944 (Ibrance 15,923, Verzenio 11,239) = 24.4%
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: atirmociclib is assumed to reach the share the third CDK4/6 entrant measurably holds, nine years after its approval and with an overall-survival label. Two assumptions sit under it. First, that the CDK4/6 class covers the whole eligible first-line pool. That overstates it, since some endocrine first-line patients take monotherapy. Second, that the beneficiary share is a first-line share. Part D beneficiaries also include second-line and, from September 2024, some adjuvant Kisqali. The case for higher: FourLight-3 is head to head against a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and Pfizer has reason to move Ibrance's 44.3% class share to a patented successor as Ibrance's negotiated Medicare price and generic entry arrive. A win would make a share well above Kisqali's plausible. The case for lower: a fourth entrant faces generic palbociclib and ribociclib by the mid-2030s
penetration_peak_pct.check: lookup.py demand 2024 Part D beneficiaries: Kisqali 8,782, Ibrance 15,923, Verzenio 11,239; 8,782/35,944 = 0.2443; Ibrance 15,923/35,944 = 0.443 as the note says. Remains a flagged judgement: a class share applied to all first-line endocrine-eligible starts, and beneficiaries mix lines. Same order as PF-07248144's 0.25
